misconception.text: A ray bends towards the normal when it enters glass from air.

correction.text: It bends away from the normal, because the speed of light is lower in glass.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: A converging lens forms an image at the same place whatever the object distance.

correction.text: The image distance changes with the object distance, and the lens equation gives it.

stem.text: Total internal reflection occurs when light passes from

options.text: a less dense to a more dense medium
a more dense to a less dense medium at an angle above the critical angle
a denser medium into the same denser medium

explanation.text: It needs a denser medium and an incident angle above the critical angle, and at that point the refracted ray disappears.

stem.text: A converging lens forms a real, inverted, magnified image when the object is placed

explanation.text: With the object beyond the focal length the image is real and inverted, and it is magnified when the object is between one and two focal lengths.

stem.text: A convex mirror always produces an image that is

explanation.text: A convex mirror always gives a virtual, upright and diminished image behind the mirror, which is why it is used as a rear view mirror.
